source.host: localhost (from .env; credentials are never recorded here)
source.reproducible: Deterministic: rows are ordered by (document, version, method, ordinal), so re-running against an unchanged database reproduces this file byte for byte, and therefore this checksum.

field_mapping.document_id: documents.public_id — e.g. 'DOC-0001'. NOT the integer key.
field_mapping.version_id: document_versions.public_id — e.g. 'VER-0001'. NOT the integer key.
field_mapping.clause_id: segments.public_id — e.g. 'CLS-0000123'. There is NO clause_id column in the schema; public_id is the identifier, and CLAUDE.md §12.3 plus backend/app/db/repository.py already expose it under the name clause_id in every API payload. Nothing is fabricated.
field_mapping.fingerprint: segments.fingerprint — 'SEG-<16 hex>', derived from (version_id, segmentation_method, ordinal) and NOT from the text. It is stable across a re-ingestion that would renumber public_id, so it is the safer join key for anything stored outside this database.
field_mapping.text: segments.text — verbatim, exactly as stored. Not normalised, re-wrapped, truncated or summarised by this export.
field_mapping.clause_number: segments.clause_number — as printed ('3.2', '(iv)'). NULL on every paragraph segment by a schema CHECK, and on clause_aware segments where no marker was detected.
field_mapping.heading: segments.heading — NULL unless a heading was detected.
field_mapping.segment_type: segments.segment_type — one of clause | paragraph | heading | annexure | preamble | unclassified.
field_mapping.segmentation_method: segments.segmentation_method — 'paragraph' or 'clause_aware'. NOT in the requested field list, but added deliberately: without it the two segmentations are indistinguishable in the file, the 138/363 split cannot be checked, and a retrieval index would silently contain the same passage twice.
field_mapping.page_end: segments.page_end — 1-based, inclusive. Equals page_start unless the segment spans a page break.
field_mapping.pages: One PageProvenance object per segment_pages row for this segment, ordered by page_number. This is the precise provenance; page_start / page_end are the cheap summary. A segment spanning two pages has TWO entries and is never collapsed onto one.
field_mapping.offset_basis: document_versions.offset_basis — which page column the character offsets index into. NOT in the requested field list, but added deliberately: the offsets are unusable without it. It is 'normalized_text' for every version in this corpus (D-11, verified), so char_start/char_end slice pages.normalized_text — NOT raw_text.

page_provenance_mapping.char_start: segment_pages.char_start — inclusive offset into that page's text on the record's offset_basis column.
page_provenance_mapping.line_index_start: segment_pages.line_index_start — 0-based line index on that page.

nullable_fields.clause_number: NULL on every paragraph segment (enforced by a schema CHECK) and on any clause_aware segment with no detected marker.
nullable_fields.heading: NULL unless a heading was detected. Rare.
nullable_fields.department / document_type / reference_n: Document-level and nullable; they live in this manifest's `documents` block, not on each record.

notes: text is verbatim from segments.text. Nothing was normalised, re-wrapped, truncated or summarised.
Both segmentations are present and cover the SAME source text. Index ONE of them — filter on segmentation_method — or the same passage will be retrieved twice.
char_start/char_end index pages.normalized_text (offset_basis), NOT raw_text. Slicing the wrong column gives the wrong span.
A segment spanning a page break has two entries in `pages`; it is never collapsed onto one page.
